title: Iran Executes Kurdish Political Prisoner Convicted for 2022 Protest Role
detail: The Islamic Republic executed 28-year-old Kurdish youth Mehrab Abdollahzadeh in Urmia Prison. He had been arrested in October 2022 during the 'Woman, Life, Freedom' uprising and sentenced to death in September 2024 on charges related to his participation in the protests. His execution was part of an accelerating pattern of capital punishment against individuals convicted for activities during the 2022 nationwide protests. Human rights organizations condemned the execution as a violation of international law, noting that Abdollahzadeh and others were sentenced to death for protest activities, not any acts of lethal violence. The execution drew protests from Kurdish diaspora communities and international human rights groups.

title: Security Forces Raid Home of Defense Attorney Asetareh Ansari
detail: Iranian security forces raided the home of attorney Asetareh Ansari, taking her into custody and transferring her to an unknown detention facility. Ansari had previously represented political prisoners and protest detainees. Her arrest was part of a broader crackdown on defense lawyers who represent prisoners arrested during the 2022 protests and those imprisoned for political activity. The systematic targeting of defense attorneys has made it increasingly difficult for political prisoners to access legal representation, drawing condemnation from bar associations and human rights organizations internationally.

title: Iran Receives US Response to 14-Point Proposal; Declares 'Ball in US Court'
detail: Iran announced it had received a US response to its 14-point peace proposal, conveyed through Pakistani intermediaries. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister stated: 'Now the ball is in the United States' court to choose the path of diplomacy or the continuation of a confrontational approach.' The exchange of proposals represented the most structured bilateral diplomatic engagement since the conflict began, though major gaps remained on nuclear enrichment, sanctions relief timelines, and the Strait of Hormuz governance framework. US officials declined to publicly confirm details of their counter-offer.
